reason: This text fragment from Nehemiah 4-5 describes the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls and the people's response to opposition. The passage contains prayers calling on God to hear them ('שְׁמַע אֱלֹהֵינוּ'), references to God frustrating the enemies' counsel ('וַיָּפֶר הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת־עֲצָתָם'), and exhortations for the people to trust God who will fight for them ('אֱלֹהֵינוּ יִלָּחֶם לָנוּ'). The passage demonstrates covenant loyalty and protection of Israel, not an absence of Yahweh's loyalty or any consideration of replacing the people with another nation. There are no theological statements suggesting either that Yahweh doesn't owe loyalty to the people or that He considers replacing them.
